title: God's Perfect Law Converts the Soul
description: God's Perfect Law Converts the Soul in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 184 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Perfection of God's Law”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God's per-fect law con-verts the soul, Re-claims from false de-sires; With sa-cred wis-dom his sure word The ig-no-rant in-spires.

lines: God's perfect law converts the soul,
With sacred wisdom his sure word
The statutes of the Lord are just,
His pure commands, in search of truth,
His perfect worship here is fixed,
His equal laws are in the scales
Of more esteem than golden mines,
More sweet than honey, or the drops

licence: Public domain: Nahum Tate died in 1715; Nicholas Brady died in 1726.
credits: Words by Nahum Tate (1652–1715) and Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
